decisions.reason: The candidate already records the independently specified J_BTN3, J_BTN4, and J_SW inputs from this message; the BOOT and J_RESET clauses belong to the separate boot/reset Requirement.
The BOOT-button placement and reset wiring do not change the selected ESP32-S3 module or its breakout requirement.

The reset connection uses EN rather than an ESP32 GPIO, and the BOOT-button clause establishes placement rather than a new GPIO assignment; unrelated GPIO clauses in the same message are not effects of the source Event.
The BOOT and reset-control decision does not alter I2C pull-ups, series resistors, bus speed, cabling, or placement.
EN in the source refers to the ESP32 reset-enable pin; it does not change the MT3608 enable connection or the GPIO5-controlled 5V rail.
J_RESET is a panel reset connection, not either of the defined power-to-main interboard connectors, so their types and pinouts remain unchanged.
An on-board development BOOT button does not change the USB-C programming interface or establish a different USB enumeration requirement.
The reset and BOOT-control details do not change the INA219 or the monitored 3.3V rail.
The source decision does not alter the standalone LDO, its activation condition, powered load, or supply-source selection.
The design clarification does not change the standing requirement that the BOM match the design, and it supplies no specific BOM-entry update for this candidate.
The BOOT and reset-control decision does not change LED supply voltage or level-shifter requirements.
The source concerns controls on the main board and panel; it does not alter the power board's dimensions, mounting, connector position, or enclosure fit.
